title: A connected étale finite-Tor lisse complex has one perfect constant value
statement:
Let $X$ be a nonempty connected scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Use the small étale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], constant sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and their derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Suppose $L\in D(X_{\mathrm{ét}},\underline R)$ has bounded cohomology, each $H^q(L)$ is locally constant with finitely generated $R$-module values [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], and there are integers $a\leq b$ such that $H^q(L\otimes_R^L F)=0$ for every degree-zero étale $R$-module sheaf $F$ and $q
otin[a,b]$ [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. Then there is a perfect ring complex $E\in D(R)$ [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex] and an étale covering $\{V_i	o X\}$ with $L|_{V_i}\simeq\underline E|_{V_i}$. For every geometric point $ ar x$ [def-weil-geometric-point, def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], $E\simeq L_{ ar x}$.

Moreover, if $W	o X$ is an affine object of the small pro-étale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] that is weakly contractible (evaluation at $W$ takes every epimorphism of sheaves of sets to a surjection) [sk-def-pe-weak-contractible], then $(
u_X^*L)|_W\simeq\underline E|_W$, where $
u_X$ is the comparison morphism [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Neither $R$ nor its finitely generated modules are required to be finite sets.

proof.text: Use boundedness directly, with the interval widened by min when necessary. Apply the declared site bounded-constant-model theorem on AsSmall of the small etale site and transport its slice restrictions and constants back. Locally constant cohomology with finite geometric stalks gives finite module values after discarding empty covering members. Exact geometric stalks identify the local derived models on intersecting images. These images are open, so the union for one isomorphism class is nonempty and clopen. Connectedness makes it all of X. This gives a cover with the single model E = the derived stalk at a chosen geometric point and identifies E with every geometric stalk. The Lean proof carries out the AsSmall transport, finite-generation transport, overlap comparison and clopen argument in private proved helpers.

Exactness identifies the cohomology of E with the geometric stalks of the cohomology of L. Thus E has bounded-above finite cohomology and is pseudo-coherent by the Noetherian criterion. Test the sheaf Tor hypothesis against the constant sheaf of each R-module N. The geometric-stalk tensor comparison and exact homology comparison give Tor amplitude [a,b] for E. Apply pseudo-coherent finite-Tor perfectness and unpack its bounded finite-projective representative to prove IsPerfectRingComplex E.
Apply the weakly contractible common-model theorem to the cover and E obtained in Step 1. This proves precisely the moreover clause, without changing E or requiring W to be connected.

Step 5 uses étale base change and the 0218 affine refinement. Step 7 shows h_U→h_W is an epimorphism by Yoneda and the sheaf equalizer axiom, then gets a section from weak contractibility and turns it into s:W→U by subcanonicity. Edge cases hold: W empty, W disconnected, R=0.
